      - article:
        - heading "Key Rule" [level=3]
        - paragraph: A Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) is a set of |V| − 1 edges that connects all vertices with minimum possible total weight and contains no cycles.
        - heading "Properties" [level=4]
        - list:
          - listitem: ✓ An MST always has |V| − 1 edges.
          - listitem: ✓ Adding any other edge creates a cycle.
          - listitem: ✓ An MST may not be unique.
        - complementary:
          - text: ⚠ Common Misconception
          - paragraph: Choosing a low-weight edge can create a cycle. Always skip edges that connect vertices already connected in your growing tree.
